notebook: Danika: a labor organizer with Sarenka connections and contact with the Kravenstal strikers.
Recommendation: predawn detention, quietly, with no press, as protective custody.
The surveillance shift changes at three forty-seven, when the house is quietest.

narrative.text: Danika brings the file herself rather than send it through channels, which is how you have learned to know a file matters before she has said a word about it.

A labor organizer, Chancellor. Sarenka connections, some contact with the Kravenstal strikers, and — according to the surveillance report — meetings with someone Voss's people flagged as Tyvaren-linked. The recommendation is a predawn detention. Quiet, no press, standard protective custody while we confirm the contact.
Protective custody. Predawn. I have read those exact words in a file before, though not one with my name on the signature line.
You ask what time. She checks the operational plan without understanding why you asked.
Three forty-seven. That's when the surveillance shift changes, so the house is quietest then. Chancellor — is something wrong?
Two men. A coat already on. A door closing slowly because they had all the time in the world. I was twelve years old at that clock face and I have never once forgotten what the hands looked like.

choices.text: Authorize it. The Tyvaren connection cannot be ignored, whatever the hour reminds you of.
Refuse it. Order a daylight interview instead, with counsel present, or no detention at all.
